about: Results of the AI editorial review for articles published with the automated label. Not a person's review.

entries.notes: Verified against Office of the Historian (parliamentary taxation milestone, saved text), National Archives Declaration transcript and Wikipedia American Revolution (wikitext re-fetched): Seven Years' War debts; GBP 133m debt, 5m of an 8m budget, 360,000 a year; Royal Proclamation of 1763 and its effects; Sugar Act 6d to 3d; Currency Act 1764; Stamp Act as first direct tax incl. playing cards; Virginia resolutions, stamp distributor's house, 9 colonies Oct 1765, 'a common cause to unite the 13 colonies'; taxes actually low; Grenville 1 vs 26 shillings; virtual representation and Otis; repeal 21 Feb 1766, Declaratory Act 'in all cases whatsoever'; Townshend duties and internal/external theory; troops 1768; Boston Massacre 5 March 1770, 11 hit, 5 died, Adams; tea duty retained 1770; Tea Party 16 Dec 1773; four Intolerable Acts; Gage removed; boycott from 1 Dec; Lexington 19 Apr 1775; Declaration grievance wording. Changed: dropped attribution of the debt figures to Middlekauff (Wikipedia cites him for an adjacent quote); vice-admiralty wording now matches source (Crown-appointed judges rather than local juries); cut the enslaved-population 'skewed comparison' claim (Wikipedia flags it citation needed) in body and FAQ and noted the 1-shilling figure excludes local taxes; replaced unsourced 'Twelve colonies' with the OOH wording (colonial legislatures sent representatives); softened molasses table row from 'close to nothing' to lax enforcement per OOH. Arithmetic (50% cut, 12 years) rechecked. Distinct intent: no other American Revolution article. check.mjs clean (top 0.015), preflight clean.

Verified against Wikipedia Origins of the American Civil War (saved text) and Yale Avalon South Carolina declaration (adopted December 24, 1860; all three quotations verbatim): 'overwhelmingly agree', 2011 panel quote, proslavery and antislavery features, 11/11 states in 1819, 36 30 line, fire bell, Compromise of 1850, Kansas-Nebraska 'all questions pertaining to slavery', firestorm, Republican Party 1854, Lecompton vote fraud, Dred Scott quote, Harpers Ferry and hanging by Virginia, martyr, Yancey $2.8bn, 1860 electoral table 180/72/39/12 with 40/18/13/30%, ten Southern ballots, Mississippi quote, six cotton states by February, Lipset 72/60/37%, states'-rights consensus, McPherson, Lost Cause negationist, Randall 'blundering generation', Shelden 4 million, Fort Sumter 12 April 1861, 75,000 militia, four states seceding. Arithmetic: 303 total, majority 152, 59.4%. Changed: 'legal across much of the country' replaced by Wikipedia wording (prevalent from 1776 to 1865, predominantly in the South); unsourced 'reignited Northern anger' replaced by an attributed Foner quote (14 words); Dred Scott wording aligned with source; electoral inference now attributed to Wikipedia (South had fewer electoral votes). Distinct intent; no other Civil War article. check clean (top 0.011), preflight clean.

Verified against Fondation Napoleon timeline (saved text) and Wikipedia Napoleon: birth 15 Aug 1769 Ajaccio, Italian origin, 1779, 1785, Toulon 1793, 13 Vendemiaire 1795, national hero, springboard; Brumaire 9 Nov 1799 details and Directory quote verbatim; constitution 13 Dec 1799 powers; Consulate institutions surviving today; Marengo 1800, Louisiana 1803; slavery abolished Feb 1794, reintroduced May 1802; Empire 18 May 1804, coronation 2 Dec 1804 with over 12,000; Austerlitz/HRE, Jena-Auerstedt, Friedland, Wagram; titles incl. King of Italy 1805; Spain 1808; 1812 force 480,000 + 120,000 (Fondation) vs ~450,000 (Wikipedia) disagreement stated, 75,000 remnant, Russian losses up to 300,000, total up to one million; Leipzig nearly 200,000 vs 300,000+; 31 Mar, 2 Apr, 6 Apr 1814; 1 Mar and 20 Mar 1815, 124,000 vs 130,000 disagreement stated, 5th Regiment joining him, 18 Jun, 22 Jun, 14 Jul, 17 Oct 1815; death 5 May 1821; autopsies, arsenic, 2021 study. Arithmetic 16.7% and 15.6% rechecked. Changed: slavery reintroduction now notes the Saint-Domingue/Guadeloupe exception; arsenic hair samples corrected from 'relatives' to 'his son and Josephine' (body and FAQ). Distinct from french-revolution-causes-and-phases. check clean (top 0.012), preflight clean.

Verified against Office of the Historian Italy page (1861 House of Savoy; Venetia and Papal States by 1871; prior relations with Sardinia, Two Sicilies and Papal States; consulates at seaports) and Wikipedia Unification of Italy (saved text plus re-fetched wikitext): Napoleonic legacy; Mazzini prison, 1831, Young Italy; Garibaldi 1834 death sentence and fourteen years in South America; Custoza 24 July 1848; Roman Republic 9 Feb 1849 and French restoration; lessons list (France paid, pope an enemy, republicanism too weak); Cavour PM 1852; Crimean War 1855; 140,000 vs 70,000; Magenta 4 June; Villafranca 12 July; annexations 22 March and Treaty of Turin 24 March 1860; a quarter of Nicard Italians; 6 May, Marsala, Calatafimi 13 May, 4,000, dictator; Naples by train 7 Sept; excommunication threat; settlement rested with Napoleon III; objective Naples not Rome; Teano; 17 March 1861; Cavour died June 1861; Custoza 24 June and Lissa 20 July 1866; 19 Oct; referendum 21-22 Oct with 69 of 642,000+ and the military-pressure caveat (0.011% rechecked); August 1870 garrison recall; Porta Pia 20 Sept with 49 soldiers + 4 officers and 19 papal troops dead; 2 Oct plebiscite; July 1871 capital; prisoner in the Vatican; 1918/Rapallo 1920 endpoint debate; Clark quote; savage insurrections. Verified against saved Wikipedia World War I text, National Archives Zimmermann Telegram page and Office of the Historian: 15-22 million deaths (range kept); 28 July, 1 August (ultimatum expiry), 2-3 August Luxembourg/France, 4 August and midnight British ultimatum; Marne, Race to the Sea, Channel-to-Switzerland trench line; Ottoman entry November 1914; Treaty of London April 1915 and Italy 23 May; chlorine at Second Ypres; Lusitania; Verdun 700,000-975,000; Somme 57,500/19,200, 420,000/200,000/500,000; Jutland; Zimmermann January / 24 Feb / 1 March, quote verbatim; 2, 4, 6 April 1917; <300,000, 667,000, 2 million; armistice December 1917, Brest-Litovsk 3 March 1918; Michael 21 March, 60 km; 15 July, 8 August; Max of Baden 3 October; Wilhelmshaven/Kiel; 9 November; Versailles 28 June 1919, Knox-Porter 2 July 1921; four dynasties. Arithmetic rechecked (1,567 days; 33%; 38,300). Changed: takeaway now says Germany and Russia were at war from 1 August (source dates the ultimatum expiry, not a declaration); Russia 'then' mobilised (source sequence); FAQ's unsupported claim that memorials give 1919 because of Knox-Porter replaced with Wikipedia's stated reason (treaty signing, troops returning). Distinct from what-started-the-first-world-war (sequence, links out for causes). App text matches catalog. check.mjs clean (top 0.012), preflight clean.

Verified against the archived CDC 1918 Pandemic page and saved Wikipedia Spanish flu text: H1N1 avian genes, 500 million infected, at least 50 million / 675,000 US; Haskell County March 1918, indeterminate origin; censorship/neutral Spain; Times quote 'Everybody thinks of it as the Spanish influenza' (late June, 3 weeks after 2 June); 75,000 v 63,000; second half of August, October peak, 292,000 v 26,000; Boston Navy Yard/Camp Devens; Philadelphia 4,597; 99% under 65; 1889-90 partial protection; 'has been contested'; estimate table 1927/1991/2005/2018; 1.8-1.9 billion, 1-6%; India 12-17 million and 1917 caveat; Russia 450,000 'shot in the dark' v 2.7 million; US 500,000-850,000 v CDC 675,000 (disagreement stated); Samoa 22% of 38,000, Tahiti 13%; non-pharmaceutical measures quote. Arithmetic rechecked (0.9%, 5.6%, 2.8%, 8,360). Changed: added John M. Barry's 2021 'well above 100 million' estimate that Wikipedia gives, so the heading, description, takeaway and table no longer cap the range at 100 million; CDC age wording aligned ('65 and older', high mortality 'in healthy people, including' 20-40, not 'died in large numbers'). History framing only, with an explicit not-medical-guidance line; no advice. App text matches catalog (disease pressure in Civilization Survival Mode; companion to coursework). check.mjs clean (top 0.014), preflight clean.

Verified against saved Library of Congress exhibition pages (overview, timeline, Constitution of 1917) and Wikipedia Mexican Revolution: 20 Nov 1910-1 Dec 1920, 'defining event' quote, around one million dead mostly non-combatants; Díaz 1876-80/1884-1911 (31 years rechecked); Creelman 1908; Madero jailed, San Antonio, Plan of San Luis Potosí; Ciudad Juárez May 1911 and treaty 21 May; Madero in office November 1911, Plan of Ayala November 1911; Katz quote; Félix Díaz and Henry Lane Wilson; February 1913 coup and killings; Carranza First Chief, Obregón; Veracruz April 1914; Aguascalientes; Celaya April 1915; US recognition October 1915; Columbus 8 soldiers + 10 civilians; Querétaro delegates (half degrees, 30% fought); 5 February 1917; articles 3, 27 (100 km/50 km), 123; Agua Prieta; 1920-1940, PRI to 2000, 'not well defined'. Changed: Huerta's resignation now gives both dates — Wikipedia mid-July 1914 v LoC timeline 15 June 1914 — and says they disagree; the end-date section and takeaway now note the LoC contradicts itself (overview 'lasting until 1917', constitution page 'culmination', timeline 'The Revolution is over' on 30 Nov 1920) v Wikipedia/Matute 1 Dec 1920; added the LoC timeline page as its own source and retitled the overview source to its real title. App text matches catalog. check.mjs clean (top 0.013), preflight clean.

Verified against saved Federal Reserve History essay and Wikipedia Great Depression: 'longest and deepest downturn' quote, August 1929 start, 1941 end, sequence of crises, March 1933 bottom and banking holiday, 1928-29 and fall 1931 rate rises via the gold standard, lender-of-last-resort failure, 'nearly 30 percent' money supply quote and equivalent price fall, real bills/liquidationist and Mellon, Bernanke 2002 quote, 'well intentioned' / 'too little and too late', reform acts, 1937 double dip; Wikipedia 15%/30%/>50%, Black Thursday 11%, Monday 12%, Tuesday 11%, 85% to 8 July 1932, Bank of United States, 608 banks/$550m, 25% / one-third farmers / 9,000 of 25,000, Smoot-Hawley 17 June 1930 and consensus with disagreement on extent, Creditanstalt May 1931, crop prices up to 60%, Congo peanuts 125 to 25 centimes, no consensus on recovery, ~15% in 1940, 1929-1939 end date (disagreement with FRH 1941 stated). Arithmetic rechecked (567%, 36%). Changed: removed invented gloss 'speculation, loose lending and falling spending' on the non-monetary camp; cut unsourced 'unusually for an institution'; German unemployment note corrected (the Germany section gives both 25% and nearly 30% in 1932, not just 25%); FAQ no longer credits Smoot-Hawley alone with the >50% trade fall. App text matches catalog (trade collapse pressure; alongside coursework). check.mjs clean (top 0.014), preflight clean.

Verified against saved Wikipedia (Causes of World War II) and Avalon Project texts: Versailles 12% land/population and 'strong currents of revanchism' verbatim; 'neither lenient enough' criticism; Articles 231/232 quotations verbatim from Avalon; Depression 'lost faith in liberal democracy'; Nazi ideology list incl. Verified against saved Wikipedia (Normandy landings) and U.S. Army D-Day history text: 'largest seaborne invasion in history' verbatim; 80 km front; 875,000 by end of June; casualties given exactly as sourced with ranges (Allied at least 10,000 incl. 4,414 confirmed dead; German 4,000-9,000; civilians ~3,000 D-Day and D+1); second-front background, planning from 1943, Eisenhower SHAEF; four candidate sites and isthmus rationale; Bodyguard/Fortitude; Rommel 18 per cent in some areas; tide/moon criteria; 5 June chosen, 4 June weather, Stagg, 18-20 June alternative, 19-22 June storm, Luftwaffe two-week storm forecast, Rommel away; Army: up to 80 percent airborne casualties, Newbury, 101st; 2,200 bombers, 24,000 airborne, 00:16 bridges, c.06:30 landings, Gold 07:25, Sword infantry 07:30, winds pushing craft east, Utah progress, house-to-house fighting; Army 'most defensible beach' quote verbatim and intelligence failure re nearly full-strength division; ineffective bombing and lost armour at Omaha; 'fewer casualties than expected'; beachheads linked 12 June, Caen 21 July; success factors. No edits needed. check.mjs clean, preflight clean.
